# Superlaunch

> Full public documentation and exact MCP input schemas.

# Superlaunch documentation

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/index

Connect your accounts, work with AI agents, and manage campaigns in Superlaunch.

Superlaunch is for performance marketers, agencies, in-house user acquisition teams, and brand owners running Meta ads. Connect your ad accounts, then use the web app or an AI assistant to analyze performance, launch creative batches, and automate campaign decisions.


  - [Set up Superlaunch](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/quickstart): Connect Meta and check your first report.
  - [Connect your AI assistant](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/connect): Set up ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, or another MCP client.


## What do you want to do?

| Task | Start here |
| --- | --- |
| Compare account, campaign, ad-set, and ad performance | [Analyze performance](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/insights) |
| Turn a batch of images and videos into ads | [Upload media](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/media), then [prepare a launch](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/launch) |
| Reuse campaign settings and schedule creative tests | [Templates](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/templates) and [recurring launches](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/schedules) |
| Pause ads or adjust budgets when conditions match | [Create and run rules](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/rules) |
| Promote successful tests or duplicate a setup | [Launch types](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/launch) and [MCP workflows](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/workflows) |
| Save brand guidance and account notes | [Brand kits](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/brands) and [Memory](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/memory) |
| Control access and review changes | [Team permissions](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/workspace/permissions) and [Activity](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/activity) |

## Current capabilities

See the [capability overview](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/reference/capabilities) for supported workflows, discovery tools, and execution limits.

## MCP reference

Developers can browse [all 104 tools](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/tools), their parameters, and [JSON examples](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/examples).

To give an assistant the documentation, use the [page index](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/llms.txt?v=20261020) or [full text](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/llms-full.txt?v=20261020).

# Current product capabilities

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/reference/capabilities

Find reporting, AutoRules, Launcher, Meta actions, memory, team access, and their MCP discovery tools.

Use this map to find supported workflows. The current reference covers 104 MCP tools. Your workspace access, enabled features, provider permissions, and account eligibility determine which operations you can use. Call the relevant discovery tool before preparing a write.

## Analyze advertising performance

Compare accounts, campaigns, ad sets, and ads. Select date ranges, daily rows or period totals, attribution, breakdowns, and metric columns. Search the column catalog, including available saved custom metrics. Use `insights_capabilities`, `insights_query`, and `insights_rank` for agent reports. Check pagination, currency, time zone, data-through dates, and warnings. See [Insights](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/insights).

## Automate decisions with AutoRules

Create, edit, archive, and run rules. Use performance conditions or a condition-free timed action. Set recurring cron timing or one exact run time, an IANA time zone, dry-run mode, and optional execution limits. Supported actions include delivery status changes, budget changes, and duplication at supported levels. Check `rules_schema` and account-specific `rules_capabilities`. See [Rules](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/rules).

## Prepare and run Launcher batches

- Upload images and videos to the shared workspace library, or import files selected through Google Drive.
- Save creative families and immutable content versions. Use exact version IDs for copy, media, language, and placement choices. Saved draft content needs no separate approval step; preview still checks eligibility.
- Organize fixed or smart collections. Save versioned templates with campaign, budget, destination, targeting, grouping, naming, and delivery settings.
- Test new creatives, promote successful tests, or refresh an existing ad set. Choose immediate, supported one-time, or recurring execution and the intended provider delivery status.
- Preview counts and budget exposure before submission. Inspect launch and operation results, retry eligible failures, or submit corrected replacement content with a new request key.

Call `launcher_discover`, `launcher_capabilities`, and `launcher_languages_list`. Resolve provider assets and existing targets with the Launcher read tools. `launcher_source_details_get` reads normalized source settings and pages of ads. `launcher_template_versions_get` reads exact retained template settings. See [Launcher](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/overview).

The content schema includes single images, single videos, carousels, collections, flexible content, existing posts, catalogs, and multilingual content. Check the specific account, objective, source assets, and preview result before choosing a format. A schema field alone does not prove live provider eligibility.

## Create, update, or duplicate Meta objects

Use direct tools for supported media uploads, creative creation, campaign/ad-set/ad creation, partial updates, duplication, and status changes. Call `actions_capabilities` first. Write tools default to dry-run mode where the schema specifies it. New campaigns, ad sets, and ads start paused.

Ad-set duplication can target another existing campaign in the same account and stays paused. Ad duplication can target an existing ad set when you supply its campaign and ad-set IDs together. Ad content updates require explicit replacement-creative policy. Check confirmed results and reconciliation warnings before retrying. See [Direct Meta actions](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/reference/actions).

## Keep brand context and shared memory

Create and edit brand profiles and structured brand kits. Store approved facts in private, workspace, brand, or ad-account memory scopes. Recall, inspect, edit, enable, disable, or delete memory through the supported tools. Save private facts only after the user asks for persistence or approves the specific save. See [Brands](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/brands) and [Memory](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/memory).

## Manage access and trace work

Invite teammates with workspace and ad-account roles. Resend or revoke pending invitations and inspect delivery status. Permissions apply to both the web app and MCP. Use OAuth to connect an AI client with read or write scopes. Review tool calls, rule runs, and provider outcomes in Activity. Check workspace billing and usage before paid operations. See [Team access](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/workspace/permissions), [MCP setup](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/connect), [Activity](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/activity), and [Billing](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/support/billing).

## Choose an interface

Use the web app for interactive setup and review. Use the [MCP tool reference](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/tools) for supported agent operations and exact input schemas. Public documentation and text exports grant no access to private workspace data. Availability in the web app does not imply a matching public HTTP endpoint or MCP tool.

# Set up Superlaunch

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/quickstart

Connect your first Meta ad account and check a report.

Connect a Meta ad account and check your first report. You need a Meta identity with access to that account. A workspace owner must connect it to Superlaunch.

## 1. Sign in and choose a workspace

Open [Superlaunch](https://app.superlaunch.pro/sign-in). Create an account or sign in, then create a workspace or accept your invitation. Complete any email verification shown during sign-in.

If you belong to more than one workspace, choose the workspace you want to use from the account menu. Connections, permissions, and billing belong to that workspace.

## 2. Connect an ad account

Open **Connections → Ad platforms**. A workspace owner can select **Connect Meta**, complete the provider authorization, and choose the accounts to connect.

Allow time for the first data import. An account can be connected before its assets and reporting data finish loading. See [Connect ad platforms](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/workspace/connections) if an account is missing.

## 3. Check a report

Open **Insights**, choose an ad account, and set a reporting period. Start with spend, impressions, and clicks. Confirm the account currency and date range before interpreting results.

An empty report can mean that the first import is still running, that the account had no delivery in that period, or that you lack reporting access.

## 4. Connect an AI assistant (optional)

Follow [Connect an MCP client](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/connect) for ChatGPT, Claude, or Codex. Approve read access for the workspace, then ask:

> List the ad accounts I can access in Superlaunch. Show their names, currencies, and time zones.

Your agent should call `ad_accounts_list` and return only accounts you can read.

## Next steps

- [Understand the account and campaign hierarchy](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/concepts/how-it-works).
- [Compare performance](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/insights).
- [Prepare your first launch](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/launch).
- [Create a rule in dry-run mode](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/rules).

# How Superlaunch works

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/concepts/how-it-works

Analyze ad performance, reuse creative work, and automate campaign tasks with your team or an AI agent.

Superlaunch helps performance marketers, agencies, in-house user acquisition teams, and brand owners manage Meta ads across multiple accounts. Use the app or an AI assistant to analyze performance, prepare campaigns, and automate routine decisions.

## Find what needs attention

Compare spend and results across campaigns, ad sets, and ads. Ask an agent questions such as “Which ads spent the most last week?” or “How did performance change by country?” Use the same reporting period when you compare results, and check how far the imported data extends.

Start with [Analyze performance](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/insights).

## Reuse your creative work

Keep images, videos, and approved copy in a shared library. Use Launcher templates to reuse campaign settings, then select the creatives for a batch or a scheduled launch. Your team can reuse the same approved content across launches.

For example, prepare several new creatives for an existing ad set, preview the planned changes, and launch them together. See [Prepare and submit a launch](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/launch).

## Automate routine checks

Create rules for conditions you would otherwise check by hand. For example, set a rule to pause an ad when its spend crosses a limit and its results do not meet your target. Run a rule manually to review its outcome, or schedule it to check while you are away.

An agent can help you [prepare a rule](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/rules). Check a dry run before enabling live changes. Submitted runs continue after you close the conversation.

## Give your team and agents controlled access

Share [brand guidance](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/brands), creative work, and account access in one workspace. Choose which workspace and scopes an agent can use when you connect it. Your team’s current permissions still determine which accounts and actions it can access.

You can use an agent for analysis while keeping campaign changes limited to the people and connections you authorize.

## See what happened

Open **Activity** to review tool calls, campaign actions, and rule runs. Check whether an operation completed, which target it affected, and whether it needs attention. A submitted request may still be running, so inspect its final result before counting the work as complete.

## Start with one task

Connect an ad account, choose a reporting period, and compare your campaigns. Then use a rule for a repeated check or Launcher for your next creative batch. You can add more accounts and invite your team as your workflow grows.

# IDs, versions, and retries

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/concepts/ids-and-versions

Use the right identifiers and avoid duplicate operations.

Resolve IDs from Superlaunch before creating or changing an object. A name helps you find an object; it does not uniquely identify it.

| Identifier | Meaning | How to obtain it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ad_account_id` | Superlaunch account UUID | `ad_accounts_list` |
| `brand_id` | Superlaunch brand UUID | `brands_list` |
| Provider campaign, ad-set, or ad ID | Object in Meta | `assets_list`, `launcher_targets_list`, or a creation result |
| Launcher creative ID | Creative family in the workspace library | `launcher_creatives_list` |
| Creative version ID | Exact saved content version | `launcher_creatives_get` |
| Template version ID | Exact saved launch settings | `launcher_templates_get` |
| Run or activity ID | Submitted work or its audit record | Submission result or activity list |

A Launcher creative ID and a Meta creative ID refer to different objects. Keep the names and IDs together while planning a launch.

## Versions

Read an object before editing it. Tools that accept `expected_version` or `expected_lock_version` require the current value from a read. If another person edits it first, refresh the object and review the change before trying again.

A saved creative or template version preserves the inputs used by an earlier launch. Saving a newer version does not rewrite those earlier inputs. Approval applies to an exact creative version.

## Request IDs and keys

For operations that advertise idempotent retries, generate one request UUID or key for one intended operation. Retry the same operation with the same inputs and key. Use a new key when the inputs or intended operation change.

Do not assume that every write tool is idempotent. Check its reference page. In particular, rule status changes and archival rely on a current version check; a supplied `request_id` does not make them replayable.

## After a timeout

Read the submitted run, action result, or [activity record](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/activity) before issuing a second write. A client timeout does not prove that the provider rejected the operation.

# Connect ad platforms

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/workspace/connections

Authorize Meta, choose accounts, and recover a disconnected connection.

Superlaunch connects to Meta through **Facebook Login for Business** and uses Meta's approved Marketing API access. A workspace owner sets up the connection; other members use the accounts their permissions allow.

## Connect Meta

1. Choose the intended workspace.
2. Open **Connections → Ad platforms**.
3. Select **Connect Meta**.
4. Sign in to Meta with an identity that can access the required ad accounts.
5. Complete the provider authorization and account selection.
6. Return to Superlaunch and check the connected accounts.

Choose only the accounts you intend to use. Your provider identity still needs the permissions required for reading reports or changing ads.

## First import

Superlaunch imports account assets and reporting data in the background. Check **Insights** after connecting. If data is missing, review the date range and allow the first import to finish.


## Reconnect

Select **Reconnect Meta** on the existing connection and complete authorization again. Reconnect after a provider authorization expires, an identity loses access, or you change the accounts available to the connection.

If an account remains missing, check that you selected the right workspace and that your Meta identity can access it. Ask the workspace owner to review account selection and member permissions.

## Agent connections

Provider connections give Superlaunch access to advertising accounts. [AI agent connections](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/connect) let an agent use Superlaunch on your behalf. Set up both if you want an agent to analyze or manage your advertising accounts.

# Team and permissions

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/workspace/permissions

Manage workspace members and control access to accounts, rules, and launches.

Your workspace owner manages members and their permissions from **Team**. The same permissions apply in the web app and through MCP.

## Invite a teammate

1. Open **Team** in the correct workspace.
2. Enter the email address the teammate will use to sign in.
3. Choose the workspace role and ad-account roles you may assign.
4. Send the invitation and check its queued, sent, or failed status.
5. Ask the teammate to accept the email link and verify their email if required.

You can resend or revoke a pending invitation. On acceptance, Superlaunch applies the saved roles after it checks current access.

Membership and account access are separate. A teammate can belong to your workspace without permission to read a particular ad account.

## Review permissions

Open the member's permissions. Grant the required functions for the relevant ad accounts, such as reading assets or insights, managing rules, or performing provider actions.

Custom metric reads need current account and Insights access. Imports and definition changes have separate account grants. A team manager can issue an API key for selected accounts and operations from **Team → API keys**. The key's issuer must keep their own access. See [Public metrics API](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/reference/custom-metrics-api).

Launcher uses its own read, author, execution, scheduling, and control permissions. Authoring a creative does not imply permission to launch it. Use the available permission definitions in the member editor.

Brand and memory access also depend on their scope. A private memory belongs to its author; team, brand, and ad-account memories follow their corresponding access rules.

## MCP access

An MCP connection uses the member who authorized it. `mcp:read` permits read tools; `mcp:write` permits write tools in addition to read access. These scopes do not expand the member's account or functional permissions.

Superlaunch rechecks membership, connection status, and target access on tool calls. If access changes, an existing conversation can lose access too.

## Resolve an access error

Check the workspace, account, member permissions, OAuth scopes, and connection status. If a rule targets several accounts, the member needs the required access to its complete target set.

See [MCP authentication](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/authentication) and [Troubleshooting](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/support/troubleshooting).

# Analyze performance

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/insights

Choose comparable dates, metrics, attribution, and reporting levels.

Use **Insights** to compare advertising performance across accounts, campaigns, ad sets, and ads.

## Build a report

1. Open **Insights** and choose the **Ad account**.
2. Set the **Reporting period**, or enter a **Start date** and **End date**.
3. Choose the entity level under **Show data for**.
4. Choose daily rows or period totals under **Show results as**.
5. Select a supported breakdown under **Break down by**.
6. For purchase analysis, choose the **Purchase type** and attribution setting under **Count purchases**.
7. Set **Sort by** and **Order** to find the results you need.

Use the same dates, conversion event, and attribution window when comparing campaigns. Check currency and time zone when comparing accounts.

## Choose report columns

Use the searchable metric checklist to choose report columns. The **Custom metrics** group shows active metrics for the selected ad account. You can put custom values beside Meta values in one report. A missing value stays empty; it is not zero. Your saved column choices remain available when you reopen Insights. See [Import custom metrics](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/custom-metrics) for setup and CSV steps.

## Use your agent

> Compare my Meta campaigns for the last seven complete days. Use purchase ROAS with the 7-day click attribution window, exclude campaigns with less than 100 in spend, and show the five highest and lowest results. Include currency, data-through date, and any warnings.

Your agent should resolve accounts, then use `insights_rank` for a compact ranking. For daily rows or breakdowns, it should call `insights_capabilities` before `insights_query`.

Structured metrics such as `actions` and `action_values` require explicit `action_types` and `attribution_windows`. The agent should ask you which event and window to use if the question leaves them unclear.

## Check completeness

The query result includes `complete` and `next_cursor`. Follow the cursor while preserving the query filters. A page of 25 rows can be only part of the report.

Use the account time zone and returned period fields when comparing dates. Check `data_through` and warnings in ranking results before treating a period as final.

# Import custom metrics

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/custom-metrics

Add daily values from a CSV file, then use them in Insights and Rules.

Custom metrics let you use daily results from your own data. Values can come from a CSV file, the public API, or MCP. All three methods use the same metric and import records.

You need access to an ad account and the **Custom metrics** import permission. To create or edit a metric, you also need the manage permission.

## Create a metric

1. Open **Custom metrics** in the Data menu.
2. Select the ad account.
3. Create a metric. Enter a key, name, description, value type, unit, and supported levels.
4. Save the metric.

Use `integer` or `decimal` for imported values. Use `count`, `currency`, or `seconds` as the unit. A metric can accept account, campaign, ad set, or ad values. Keep one meaning for each metric key. If its meaning changes, create a new metric.

Calculated metrics use the `amount_per_count` or `amount_per_spend` template. Import their additive parts. The system calculates the ratio from totals.

## Import a CSV file

1. Select **Download CSV template** for the current account. The template includes active metric keys and account fields.
2. Enter one value for each metric, entity, and closed account date. Enter an exact decimal in the `value` column. A blank value is invalid.
3. Select **Upload values**, then select the CSV file.
4. Select **Prepare import**. Check row errors and the preview of current and new values.
5. Select **Commit import** when the preview is valid.

Preparation does not change values. Commit creates a task. The task page shows its ID, file, status, row counts, and confirmed progress. You can leave the page and return through **Import history**. When the task completes, select **Open in Insights**. If the file has more than one entity level, select the level first.

A supplied `0` is a value. A missing row is unknown. A later import replaces the same metric, entity, and date. Dates that you omit stay unchanged.

Only one import can run for an ad account at a time. A failed task can leave some values applied. Check its confirmed counts. Prepare a new import to correct those values.

## Read the values

In **Insights**, open the metric selector and choose the **Custom metrics** group. Select custom and Meta metrics in the same report. Use the account, entity level, and date filters. A missing value stays empty.

You can also use a custom metric in a Rule. Rules use closed account dates and check all required custom inputs before they select a task. A missing input cannot pass through an `OR` condition or a fallback task. During an active or failed import, a Rule reads the current stored values. Run a new Rule in dry-run mode and check its decisions before you enable live actions.

## Use another input method

- [Public metrics API](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/reference/custom-metrics-api) covers API keys, JSON and CSV preparation, commit, task status, and queries.
- [Custom metric MCP tools](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/reference/custom-metrics) lists the tool arguments and input schemas. A fresh authorized MCP client can discover all 11 tools.

## Access and history

The metric and its values belong to one team and ad account. Reads require current account and Insights access. Imports and definition changes need their own grants. An archived metric keeps its stored values and history. An active calculated metric or enabled Rule can block archive.

Import history keeps the task ID and result. An operator retention command can expire unused previews after 24 hours. It can clear old task payloads after 7 or 90 days, based on task status. Current metric values remain available.

# Public metrics API

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/reference/custom-metrics-api

Create metric definitions, import values, check tasks, and query results with a team API key.

Use the public metrics API for scheduled imports and reads. The routes start with `/api/public`. They use the same metric definitions and import tasks as the Superlaunch app and MCP tools.

## Get an API key

In **Team → API keys**, create a key. Select its allowed ad accounts, permissions, and expiry. Copy the secret when it appears. It is shown once.

Send `Authorization: Bearer <metric_api_key>` on public requests. A key can act only on its explicit account list. The issuer must still have access to each account. Expiry, revocation, or loss of access stops new requests. A key cannot call unrelated API routes or manage API keys.

Use `GET /api/public/ad-accounts` to find the internal ad account UUID. Keep it separate from the provider account ID.

## Routes

| Task | Route |
| --- | --- |
| Find allowed accounts | `GET /api/public/ad-accounts` |
| List or create metrics | `GET /api/public/custom-metrics` or `POST /api/public/custom-metrics` |
| Read or edit one metric | `GET /api/public/custom-metrics/{metric_id}` or `PATCH /api/public/custom-metrics/{metric_id}` |
| Download the current CSV template | `GET /api/public/custom-metrics/template.csv` |
| Prepare JSON rows | `POST /api/public/custom-metric-imports` |
| Prepare a CSV file | `POST /api/public/custom-metric-imports/file` |
| List imports or read one task | `GET /api/public/custom-metric-imports` or `GET /api/public/custom-metric-imports/{import_id}` |
| Commit a valid task | `POST /api/public/custom-metric-imports/{import_id}/commit` |
| Create a CSV upload grant | `POST /api/public/custom-metric-upload-grants` |
| Send CSV bytes with a grant | `PUT /api/public/custom-metric-uploads/{upload_id}` |
| Query values | `POST /api/public/metrics/query` |

List routes use a bounded page and an opaque `cursor`. Keep the account and filters the same when you request the next page.

## Prepare and commit values

Send the ad account UUID, an idempotency key, and daily rows. The example IDs are placeholders. Replace them with IDs that you can access.

```json
{
  "ad_account_id": "10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "idempotency_key": "crm-export-2026-10-23",
  "rows": [
    {
      "metric_id": "20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
      "entity_level": "campaign",
      "entity_id": "120000000001",
      "date": "2026-10-23",
      "value": "30"
    }
  ]
}
```

The `value` field is a decimal string. Use a closed date in the ad account time zone. A zero value is `"0"`. A missing row leaves the stored value unchanged.

The prepare response has a `task_id`, preview, and bounded errors. Preparation does not write daily values. Check the preview. Commit a valid task with `POST /api/public/custom-metric-imports/{import_id}/commit?ad_account_id=<account_uuid>`. A new accepted task returns HTTP `202`. Read the same task ID until its status is `completed` or `failed`.

The same idempotency key and payload return the same task. The same key with different data returns a conflict. A failed task can have some values applied. Read its counts before you prepare a correction.

For a CSV file, use the multipart prepare route with the current template. A signed upload grant provides another CSV path for clients that cannot use multipart. Upload prepares the task; it does not commit it.

## Query values

Send `ad_account_id`, `entity_level`, `metric_refs`, `date_from`, and `date_to` to `POST /api/public/metrics/query`. Use `custom:<metric_uuid>` for a custom metric. You can include supported provider metrics in the same request. Select `daily` or `period` grain. Follow the response cursor for more rows.

A query reads current stored values. It can include some corrections from an active or failed import. A missing value stays null. The query checks current account and read access.

See [Import custom metrics](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/custom-metrics) for the app flow and [Custom metric MCP tools](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/reference/custom-metrics) for agent calls.

# Create and run rules

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/rules

Define targets, conditions, actions, schedules, and dry-run checks.

Use a rule to check campaign performance and apply an action on a schedule. For example, pause ads that spend above your limit without a purchase.

## Create a rule

1. Open **Rules** and select **New rule**.
2. Select the ad accounts and target level.
3. Add a target filter, or choose an empty filter to cover the selected level.
4. Add a task with at least one action. Add conditions when the action depends on performance.
5. For each condition, set the metric, timeframe, operator, and comparison value.
6. Choose a recurring schedule or one exact run time, then set the time zone.
7. Save as a draft with dry-run mode enabled.

Use **Active items only** to limit a task to active objects. Turn it off if you need the rule to consider paused objects too.

Budget-increase actions require a maximum daily budget; budget-decrease actions require a minimum. Absolute adjustments and rule safety bounds use major account-currency units. Direct creation tools use minor units instead.

## Use custom metrics

Select an active custom metric for the Rule's ad account and target level. Custom metrics use closed account dates. The Rule checks that every required custom value exists before it selects a task. A missing value cannot pass through an `OR` condition or a fallback task. An explicit zero is a value.

An import in progress or a failed import does not stop the Rule. The Rule reads current stored values, which can include some corrections from that import. Check the import task and use dry-run mode when you test a new Rule. See [Import custom metrics](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/custom-metrics).

## Check a dry run

Run the current rule version with `dry_run: true`. Review which objects match and which actions the rule would take before allowing live changes.

> Draft a rule for this account that pauses active ads when spend exceeds 50 today and purchases are zero. Use dry-run mode, show the target filter and schedule, and wait for me to review before activation.

Your agent should call `rules_schema` for the rule vocabulary and `rules_capabilities` for the selected account and level. Recorded event availability does not prove that Meta accepts the event for optimization. It should obtain the account ID and ask for any missing targeting or scheduling choices.

## Timed actions and duplication

A task can have an empty top-level condition group when you want a scheduled action without metric checks. Through MCP, use `schedule.cron` for recurring work or `schedule.run_at` for one exact time with a UTC offset. Choose one mode and supply an IANA time zone.

Duplication rules can copy campaigns, ad sets, or ads. An ad-set rule can use a destination campaign in the same account and creates paused copies. An ad rule requires both destination campaign and ad-set IDs. Check the source level, destination, delivery status, and optional execution limit before activation.

## Edit or activate

Read the rule's current version before changing it. `rules_update` replaces the definition, so preserve fields you intend to keep.

To allow scheduled live changes, set the rule to **Active** and turn off **Dry run**. Review both settings before saving. A manual MCP `rules_run` defaults to dry-run mode.

## Review results

Open the run details or use `rule_runs_get`. Review [Activity](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/activity) for decisions and provider actions. `rules_delete` archives the rule.

# Review activity and results

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/activity

Trace tool calls, provider actions, and rule runs to their outcomes.

Open **Activity** to review operations in your workspace. Use it after an agent write, a rule run, or a failed request.

## Find an operation

Filter by member, tool, action, account, rule, or status. A request or run ID helps you find a specific operation. Open the record to inspect its parameters, result, timing, and error code.

An accepted request can still be pending. Report a provider change as successful only after its result confirms that change.

## Through MCP

Use `activity_list` to search the unified log. Exact filters work for known fields; `query` searches text across tool, action, member, target, request, and error metadata.

Use `activity_get` for one complete record and `activity_summary` to count the complete filtered result set. Follow `next_cursor` until `complete` is true when you need the full list.

The `rule_activity_*` tools return rule-specific activity. They do not replace the unified log for all tool and action operations.

## Investigate a failure

1. Find the request's activity record.
2. Check the account and target IDs.
3. Read the error code and result.
4. Check related run or action records.
5. Resolve authorization or input errors before retrying.

After a timeout, read the result before submitting another provider write. For a Launcher batch, inspect [operation-level results](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/recovery) so that you retry only eligible failed work.

# Brand profiles and kits

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/brands

Give your team and agent the brand guidance they need.

Use **Brands** to keep a brand profile and structured kit in your workspace.

## Create a profile

Open **Brands** and select **New brand**. Add the name, website, industry, description, markets, and languages that apply. Save the profile, then open **Edit brand** to add its kit.

Creating a brand through MCP does not link ad accounts. Treat account assignment as a separate setup task.

## Add a brand kit

Use the kit to record:

- **Main message**: the brand's positioning.
- **Tagline** and supporting proof points.
- Colors with roles such as primary, accent, background, and text.
- Heading and body fonts.
- Voice traits and writing guidance.

Use concrete guidance, such as “Use short sentences and describe the product's function before its benefits.” Give your agent verified proof points instead of claims it must infer.

## Use the kit through MCP

`brands_list` finds the profile and `brands_get` returns its active kit. Ask your agent to read it before writing campaign copy.

> Read the brand kit for this brand. Draft three ad headlines using its main message and voice guidance. Use only the supporting claims in the kit.

`brands_update` accepts partial updates. Omitted fields keep their values; empty lists clear list fields. A changed kit creates a new immutable version. When no active kit exists, the kit needs `positioning`.

Brand kits hold structured brand guidance. Use [Memory](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/memory) for additional facts you explicitly want to retain.

# Save and manage memory

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/memory

Save facts for later conversations and choose who can use them.

Memory stores facts you want to reuse in later conversations. Save a fact when you ask your agent to remember it or approve a focused suggestion to save it.

## Choose a scope

| Scope | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| Private | Your personal working preferences |
| Team | Facts relevant to the workspace |
| Brand | Guidance specific to a brand |
| Ad account | Facts specific to an advertising account |

Brand and ad-account scopes require the corresponding Superlaunch UUID. Private and team scopes do not take a target ID.

## Save a fact

> Remember for this brand that campaign copy must use British English and avoid discount claims unless I provide an approved offer.

The agent should confirm whether it saved the fact. If the fact is still processing, it may take time to appear in search.

Developers: `memory_remember` requires the fact, scope, a request UUID, and consent. See [Memory tools](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/reference/memory) for the possible results.

## Review and correct

Open **Memory** to review available records. Through MCP, `memory_list` lists records and `memory_get` reads an exact record. `memory_recall` finds relevant context for a query.

Read the current version before using `memory_update`, `memory_set_enabled`, or `memory_forget`. Disable a record to stop future retrieval; forget it when you want permanent deletion.

## Interpret recalled facts

Review recalled facts if your plans or brand guidance have changed. Update outdated facts so that later conversations use the right information. Your current instructions take precedence over saved memory.

# Launcher overview

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/overview

Save creative versions, reuse campaign settings, and run immediate or scheduled launches.

Launcher creates campaigns and ads from your workspace's creative library. Use it to prepare batches, reuse campaign settings, schedule work, and inspect provider results.

## The building blocks

| Object | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Media | Uploaded or imported image or video |
| Creative | A named family of content with saved versions |
| Saved creative version | Exact content selected for a launch |
| Collection | A fixed selection or smart filter over creatives |
| Template version | Saved campaign, ad-set, budget, and naming settings |
| Launch | Submitted work with recorded inputs and operation results |
| Schedule | Recurring launch configuration and limits |

The library belongs to the workspace. Launches target an ad account. Authoring, execution, scheduling, and control require their respective permissions. Account limits cap the campaigns and configured budgets that Launcher can create; they are not a cap on all Meta account spend.

## Prepare and launch

1. [Upload or import media](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/media).
2. [Save a creative version](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/creatives).
3. [Create a template](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/templates).
4. Select creatives or a [collection](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/collections).
5. [Prepare and submit a launch](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/launch).
6. Inspect its [results and recovery options](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/recovery).

Through MCP, call `launcher_discover` to check available tools, limits, and setup requirements. Use `launcher_capabilities` for account policy and `launcher_languages_list` for supported language identities. Preview checks current provider eligibility.

## Preview and usage

A preview estimates selected creatives, writes, budget exposure, and usage. It reserves nothing. Submission checks saved content eligibility, access, billing, and limits again.

Superlaunch records usage for confirmed changes in Meta. Check **Billing** for your allowance and recorded usage.

# Upload and import media

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/media

Add images and videos to the shared library or import selected Drive files.

Add images and videos under **Launcher → Creatives → Import media**, then use them in a [creative](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/creatives).

## Upload a file

1. Select **Upload files** and choose an image or video.
2. Select **Upload selected file**.
3. Keep the page open until the upload finishes.
4. Check the media item's status and preview before using it.

The upload control shows the file types and size limits. If a thumbnail fails, check the media status and retry the thumbnail before uploading the file again.

## Import from Google Drive

1. Select **Import from Google Drive**.
2. Connect your Google account if prompted.
3. Select the files you want to make available to Superlaunch.
4. Review the selection and select **Import selected files**.
5. Check the results for files that need another attempt.

Superlaunch can read files you select through Google Picker. Selecting a folder does not give access to all its files or start an import. Select each new batch of files before refreshing the folder browser.

## Upload through an AI client

Clients that support the Superlaunch upload picker can accept up to ten files per batch, with a default combined limit of 64 MiB. Ask your assistant to upload your images or videos to the workspace library.

If your client cannot show the picker, use the browser steps above. The assistant can find saved files with `launcher_media_list` and read their details with `launcher_media_get`.

Developers can also use the [signed upload workflow](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/workflows) and [media tool reference](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/reference/actions).

# Create and version creatives

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/creatives

Save immutable content versions, select exact versions, and review their media.

A creative contains your ad copy and media. Superlaunch saves content edits as separate versions so you can select and launch specific content. The tools call the parent creative a **creative family**.

## Create a creative

1. Open **Launcher → Creatives → Library**.
2. Select **New creative**.
3. Enter a name and the organizing fields you need.
4. Choose the supported format and language.
5. Add the message, headline, destination, and required identity fields.
6. Choose saved media for the format and any supported placement variants.
7. Save the creative and inspect its version.

The content schema includes single images, single videos, carousels, collections, flexible ads, existing posts, and catalogs. Multilingual content and placement media use saved variant and slot assignments. Schema support does not guarantee that an account, objective, or placement can launch a format. Use account capabilities and preview to check the exact combination.

## Select a saved version

Saved draft content is eligible for launch checks. You do not need a separate approval step. Inspect the copy, media, language, and destination before submitting a launch.

Content edits create a new immutable version. Use `launcher_creatives_get` to page through saved version summaries and `launcher_creative_versions_get` to read exact content. Pin `creative_id` and `creative_version_id` pairs in `selection.creative_versions`. You can select distinct versions of one creative in the same launch.

## Revoke or archive

Revoke a version when you need to prevent its selection. Archive the family when you want to remove it from active library use.

Earlier launches retain their recorded content inputs. Revocation does not rewrite provider objects created by earlier launches.

## Check usage

Use the creative's usage view or `launcher_creatives_usage` to find launches that used it. Read `launcher_creatives_get` or `launcher_creative_versions_get` when you need exact version details.

# Organize collections

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/collections

Use fixed selections or smart filters to choose creatives for launches.

Collections help you reuse a selection of creatives.

## Choose a collection kind

A **fixed collection** contains the creative families you select. Use it for a specific campaign or a set you have reviewed.

A **smart collection** uses filters such as name, concept, saved language, saved format, tags, source, or import date. A creative must match all conditions, but it can match any value within one condition. Add exclusions if a matching creative should stay out.

## Create a collection

1. Open **Launcher → Creatives → Collections**.
2. Create a collection and enter its name.
3. Choose fixed or smart selection.
4. Add members or filters.
5. Review the selected or matching creatives.
6. Select **Save collection**.

Smart-filter previews show current matches. Launch preparation still checks which exact saved versions are eligible.

## Resolve a launch selection

Use the resolve-selection control or `launcher_collections_resolve` to obtain a selection for a launch. Check exclusions and rejected items before submission.

A submitted launch keeps the creative versions you selected, even if you edit the library later.

## Edit or archive

Read the current collection before editing or archiving it through MCP. Use its current lock version where required. For scheduled selection behavior, see [Recurring launches](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/schedules).

# Create launch templates

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/templates

Save versioned campaign settings, budgets, destinations, and naming.

A template holds settings you can reuse across launches. Saving an edit creates a new template version; earlier launches keep the settings they used.

## Create a template

Open **Launcher → Templates** and select **Create template**. Set:

- Campaign objective and budget ownership.
- Daily or lifetime budget, currency, and amount.
- Destination, optimization goal, billing event, and promotion details.
- Targeting and delivery settings.
- Allowed creative formats and language mode.
- Grouping and object naming.

Use the available selectors for provider objects such as Pages and promotion assets. Resolve exact IDs instead of entering an object name as an ID. Through MCP, use `launcher_assets_list` and follow its parent requirements and cursors. Pages and Instagram accounts come from synced data; check `sync_status` and `synced_at`. Other asset kinds use live provider discovery.

## Budget and delivery

Confirm that the budget currency matches the account. The web interface accepts displayed currency amounts; MCP fields ending in `_minor` use integer minor units. For USD, `1000` means $10.00.

Review bid strategy, bid amount, or ROAS constraints where the chosen objective requires them. A ROAS value is a ratio, not a currency amount.

Set the delivery time zone before entering start and end times. A launch schedule controls when Superlaunch starts work; template delivery settings control the provider's delivery times.

## Reuse or revise

Save the template and choose the version during [launch setup](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/launch). Through MCP, use `launcher_templates_get` to inspect its versions, `launcher_template_versions_get` to read an exact retained version, and `launcher_template_versions_create` to save new settings.

Archive a template to remove it from active use. Keep earlier version IDs when reviewing an existing launch or schedule.

# Prepare and submit a launch

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/launch

Select an operation, saved content, target, timing, and delivery status.

Before you submit, confirm the workspace, ad account, saved creative versions, and campaign settings. A launch can create campaigns and ads in Meta and count toward your workspace usage.

## Choose an operation

Choose a **Launch type**:

| Launch type | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| Test new creatives | Create a test from saved library content |
| Promote successful tests | Use results from earlier tests in a new campaign or an existing ad set |
| Refresh an existing ad set | Add creatives to an ad set you select |

For an existing ad set, review its current settings before submitting. Use `launcher_source_details_get` to read normalized source settings and page through source ads. Use the returned IDs and follow `next_cursor`.

Through MCP, call `launcher_discover`, resolve accounts, and use `launcher_targets_list` followed by `launcher_targets_get` when an existing target is required.

## Prepare the inputs

1. Open **Launcher** and choose the ad account.
2. Select **New launch** and enter a **Launch name**.
3. Select the operation and template version. Pin exact saved creative versions when you need specific content.
4. Choose creatives or resolve a collection.
5. Review grouping, budget, and targeting.
6. Choose the launch time. Recurring timing is available for **Test new creatives**.
7. Choose **Create paused** or **Activate after creation**.

Activation can start delivery and spend. Confirm that choice before submission.

## Preview

Select **Preview (optional)** to check the planned Meta objects, names, estimated usage, and configured budgets. Meta can still reject a request at submission or execution.

Correct missing inputs and review the selection. Submission checks permissions, saved content eligibility, provider state, billing, and limits again.

## Version reuse

Use `selection.creative_versions` to pin exact versions. Use `manual_groups.creative_version_ids` for explicit grouping. Selecting another saved version needs no retest reason. Reusing the same confirmed version requires `retest_reason`; held or uncertain usage cannot be retested. Read current usage before submitting.

## Submit and track

Submit the launch once. Your agent should use one stable `request_key` for the intended operation and retain the returned launch ID.

Read `launcher_launches_get` and `launcher_run_operations` until you understand the final outcome. A batch can contain both successful and failed operations. See [Recover a launch](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/recovery).

# Schedule recurring launches

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/schedules

Set recurring timing, selection behavior, and batch limits.

A recurring schedule prepares launches from saved configuration. You need scheduling access as well as the permissions required for the launch.

## Create a schedule

1. Open launch setup.
2. Choose **Test new creatives** and a saved template version.
3. Choose a collection and review its selection behavior.
4. Select recurring timing.
5. Set the frequency, time, and **Schedule time zone**.
6. Set the batch count and budget limits.
7. Review whether created objects stay paused or activate.
8. Save the schedule.

The schedule time zone determines when the recurring job starts. Provider delivery settings in the template are separate.

## Check saved settings

The schedule uses specific template and collection versions. Review them before saving; editing a template later does not update the version selected by the schedule. Runs that have already started keep their original settings.

Superlaunch skips overlapping and missed runs. Each new run checks saved creative eligibility, access, billing, and limits before launching.

## Pause, edit, and inspect

Open the schedule to inspect its current status and recent work. Read its lock version before an MCP update. Use `launcher_schedules_change_status` to change status and `launcher_schedules_update` to revise configuration.

Read the resulting launch and operation records after an occurrence. If it fails, review the reason before re-enabling or retrying.

See [Launcher MCP tools](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/reference/launcher-schedules) for exact schedule fields.

# Inspect and recover launches

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/recovery

Understand partial results and choose retries or replacement work.

A submitted launch can succeed, fail, or finish with only some operations complete. Inspect operation results before deciding how to recover it.

## Inspect the result

Open the launch in **Launcher**. Review operation status, provider object IDs, error codes, and suggested recovery steps.

Through MCP, read `launcher_launches_get`, then `launcher_run_operations`. Use the result's available operations and recovery guidance instead of guessing from a status label.

## Retry unchanged work

Use `launcher_launches_retry` only for operations that the current result identifies as eligible. Retain the original inputs for that work and use the request fields required by the retry tool.

Successful provider writes already exist. Avoid resubmitting the entire batch to address one failed item.

## Replace corrected content

To fix a failed item's content, save a corrected creative version. Through MCP, use `launcher_launches_replacement_candidates` to find items eligible for replacement. Submit the corrected version with the returned replacement details, the target ad set, and a new request key.

Preview the corrected selection and inspect the fresh target before submission. Changed content is a new operation.

## Cancel or hold a launch

Use `launcher_launches_cancel` to request cancellation. Use `launcher_launches_change_status` to hold or resume an unstarted launch; it does not set the delivery status of existing provider ads. A missed launch time requires Run now or a new time.

A cancellation request does not erase provider objects or guarantee that a write already underway stops. Read the resulting state and account activity.

# Superlaunch MCP

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/overview

Connect an AI client to your workspace's advertising data and operations.

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets an AI client discover and call Superlaunch tools. Use it to inspect accounts, analyze performance, prepare launches, manage rules, and use your saved brand guidance.

## Server connection

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Server URL | `https://mcp.superlaunch.pro/mcp` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP |
| Authentication | OAuth |
| Client registration | Automatic dynamic client registration |
| Read scope | `mcp:read` |
| Write scope | `mcp:write` |

Sign in through the browser, choose a workspace, and approve access. Your agent uses the resulting connection on your behalf. You do not paste your Superlaunch password or provider credentials into the conversation.

## Supported work

- Read authorized ad accounts, brands, assets, and insights.
- Create and manage rules and inspect their runs.
- Create, duplicate, or change supported Meta objects.
- Prepare Launcher library content, collections, templates, launches, and schedules.
- Save approved facts and retrieve relevant memory.
- Review unified activity and operation results.

The tool catalog can vary with approved scopes and feature availability. Use capability tools before preparing actions.

## Get started

[Connect your client](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/connect), then use [Your first MCP workflow](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/first-workflow). The [tool index](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/tools) lists the documented methods by task.

## Give an assistant the documentation

Use [/llms.txt](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/llms.txt?v=20261014) to find pages or [/llms-full.txt](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/llms-full.txt?v=20261014) for the full text. To read your account data, the assistant also needs the product connection above.

# Connect an MCP client

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/connect

Set up Superlaunch in ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, or another OAuth client.

You need a Superlaunch workspace and an AI client that supports remote MCP with OAuth. Use this server URL:

```text
https://mcp.superlaunch.pro/mcp
```


## ChatGPT Work

1. Open the **Plugins** directory in ChatGPT.
2. Select **+ → Add custom MCP server**.
3. Name it **Superlaunch** and enter the server URL.
4. Choose **OAuth** with dynamic client registration. Leave client ID and secret empty.
5. Review the access notice, create the plugin, and install it from your personal plugins.
6. Sign in to Superlaunch, choose a workspace, and approve access.
7. Start a **Work** chat. Type `@` and select Superlaunch.

See the [official plugin connection guide](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/quickstart). If your ChatGPT workspace uses the Apps interface, use **Apps → Create**, enable developer mode where required, enter the same OAuth server, and complete the tool scan. Availability and admin controls depend on the ChatGPT plan; check the [official MCP app guide](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-developer-mode-and-mcp-apps-in-chatgpt).

## Claude

1. Open **Customize → Connectors**.
2. Select **+ Add → Add custom connector**.
3. Name it **Superlaunch**, enter the URL, and continue.
4. Choose sign-in authentication and **Register automatically** for the OAuth client.
5. Add the connector, sign in to Superlaunch, choose a workspace, and approve access.
6. In the conversation, open **+ → Connectors** and enable Superlaunch.

A Team or Enterprise organization may require an owner to add the connector first. See [Claude's remote connector guide](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp).

## Codex CLI

```bash
codex mcp add superlaunch --url https://mcp.superlaunch.pro/mcp
codex mcp login superlaunch
```

Complete authorization in the browser. Start a new session and use `/mcp` to check the connection. Run `codex mcp list` to inspect configured servers. See the [official MCP guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli).

## Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http superlaunch https://mcp.superlaunch.pro/mcp
```

Start Claude Code, run `/mcp`, and complete OAuth authentication. See the [official Claude Code MCP guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp).

## Other clients

Add a remote Streamable HTTP server, enter the URL, and choose OAuth with automatic registration. Complete browser authorization and enable the connection. Ask the client to list the available tools, then run `ad_accounts_list`.

## Verify and disconnect

Open **Connections → AI agents** in Superlaunch. Check that the connection appears and that a tool call updates its activity.

Select **Disconnect** to revoke it. Reconnect through your client when you want to authorize it again.

# Authentication and access

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/authentication

Understand OAuth scopes, workspace selection, and revocation.

Superlaunch's product MCP endpoint requires OAuth authorization. Each connection belongs to the member and workspace selected during consent.

## Authorize access

Start the connection in your MCP client. Sign in to Superlaunch in the browser, choose the workspace, and review the requested scopes.

- `mcp:read` permits read tools.
- `mcp:write` permits write tools and requires read scope.

Selecting write scope does not grant new provider or account permissions. Superlaunch checks the connection, workspace membership, function, and referenced objects when you call a tool.

## Workspace selection

Authorize the workspace you intend the agent to use. Switching workspaces in the web application does not redefine the workspace attached to an existing MCP authorization.

If you need a different workspace, reconnect and choose it during consent. Confirm the returned account list before an operation.

## Discovery for client developers

The public protected-resource metadata is available at:

```text
https://mcp.superlaunch.pro/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp
```

It identifies the resource `https://mcp.superlaunch.pro/mcp`, the authorization server `https://auth.superlaunch.pro/`, and the supported scopes. Use your MCP client's OAuth implementation for registration, authorization, token refresh, and bearer headers.

An unauthenticated request returning HTTP 401 is expected. Adding the URL alone does not authorize access.

## Revoke access

Open **Connections → AI agents** and select **Disconnect**. Superlaunch rechecks revoked connections on calls. Removing an agent from a conversation and revoking its Superlaunch connection are separate actions.

See [MCP troubleshooting](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/troubleshooting) if authorization loops or a tool becomes unavailable.

# Your first MCP workflow

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/first-workflow

Verify access and ask your agent for a read-only performance check.

[Connect your client](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/connect), then ask your assistant to check campaign performance. This exercise reads reports without changing ads.

## 1. Choose an account

> Use Superlaunch to list the ad accounts I can access. Include their names, currencies, and time zones.

Choose an account from the result. If two accounts have the same name, ask for their IDs to identify the right one.

## 2. Ask for a report

> For this account, show daily campaign spend, impressions, and clicks for the last seven complete days. Check which metrics Superlaunch supports first. State the dates, currency, and time zone, and tell me if any results are missing.

The assistant uses `insights_capabilities` to check supported reports, then `insights_query` to read the data. If the result spans several pages, it needs to read each page before presenting a complete report.

## 3. Check the answer

Confirm that the report uses the account and dates you selected. Ask the assistant to explain any missing data or warnings before drawing conclusions.

You can follow up with:

> Which campaigns had the highest spend? Show their clicks and impressions alongside spend.

For conversion analysis, specify the event and attribution window. See [Analyze performance](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/insights).

## Next steps

Try a [rule, launch, or memory workflow](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/workflows). Developers can use the [JSON argument examples](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/examples) and [tool reference](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/tools).

# MCP workflows

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/workflows

Use discovery, validation, writes, and result checks in the right order.

Start a workflow by discovering accessible objects and capabilities. Resolve required IDs, review the proposed change, submit it, then inspect the result.

## Rank campaign performance

1. Call `ad_accounts_list`.
2. Choose the accounts, dates, conversion event, and attribution window.
3. Use `insights_rank` for compact highest and lowest rankings.
4. Read the data-through date and warnings.

Set a minimum spend or conversion count to exclude results with too little data. For cost metrics such as CPA, lower values can be better.

## Import custom values

Call `custom_metrics_list` to find an account metric. Prepare a small set of values with `custom_metrics_import_prepare`. For a CSV file, use `custom_metrics_upload_create` and upload the bytes with its signed grant. Read the preview with `custom_metrics_import_get`. Commit a valid task with `custom_metrics_import_commit`, then poll the same task ID. A failed task can leave some values applied. See [Import custom metrics](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/custom-metrics) and [Custom metric tools](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/reference/custom-metrics).

## Create a draft rule

Call `rules_schema`, resolve accounts, and build the full rule definition. Supply a target filter, tasks with actions and optional conditions, and a schedule with time zone. Save as a draft with `dry_run: true`.

Read the rule back and run its current version in dry-run mode. Review decisions before activation. See [Rules](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/guides/rules).

## Prepare a Launcher batch

Call `launcher_discover`, choose an account, and inspect saved creatives and templates. [Upload or import media](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/media) if you need new files.

Select exact saved creative versions, resolve the selection, inspect an existing target where required, and preview the launch. Submit with one stable request key. Poll the launch and operation records, including partial failures.

## Create Meta objects directly

Call `actions_capabilities` to check whether live changes are enabled. Creation and duplication tools default to `dry_run: true`; creation starts campaigns, ad sets, and ads paused.

For media, call `media_uploads_create` to open the upload picker when your client supports it. `media_uploads_complete` uploads one to ten selected files and returns a result for each file. Check those results before using the media.

For a signed upload without the picker, provide file metadata to `media_uploads_create`. Upload the file bytes using the returned URL, method, and headers before the URL expires. A successful upload saves the file in the workspace library. Use `media_asset_id` with Launcher tools or `media_id` with `creatives_create`.

Create a campaign, then an ad set, then an ad with the required parent IDs. Review dry-run results. Use a new request ID when changing the request from validation to live execution. Inspect the action result after execution.

## Reuse a successful setup

Use `campaigns_duplicate`, `adsets_duplicate`, or `ads_duplicate` to copy an existing Meta setup. Copies stay in the source account. An ad-set copy can target an existing campaign through `destination_campaign_id`; omit it to keep the source campaign. Ad-set copies stay paused. An ad copy can target an existing ad set when you supply its campaign and ad-set IDs together. Ad copies default to paused; an active copy requires an explicit status choice.

To use a setup in a different account, prepare a new launch with that account's assets and compatible template settings. Check its currency, Pages, pixels, audiences, and permissions before submitting.

For successful Launcher tests, choose **Promote successful tests** and select the source ads. See [Prepare and submit a launch](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/launcher/launch).

## Update existing Meta objects

Use `campaigns_update`, `adsets_update`, or `ads_update` for supported partial changes. Read the current object, select only the fields you intend to change, and run a dry run first. Budget values use account-currency minor units.

Ad content edits require `creative_policy: "replace"`. New creative content can trigger provider review and does not preserve the existing post engagement. Inspect the returned verification state: `simulation`, `confirmed`, or `reconciliation_required`. Read results before retrying an uncertain write.

## Save a confirmed fact

Resolve the scope, then call `memory_remember` only after an explicit save request or focused approval. Report the returned persistence state. Use `memory_recall` for relevant context and `memory_get` for an exact record.

# MCP troubleshooting

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/troubleshooting

Resolve connection, permission, input, and result-completeness problems.

Use the symptom below to choose the next check.

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Server asks you to sign in | Complete OAuth in the browser; the URL alone is not authorization |
| No tools in the conversation | Enable the connector or plugin in that conversation, then refresh tool discovery |
| Read tools appear but writes do not | Check approved `mcp:write` scope and your client's action restrictions |
| Account not found | Confirm workspace, account ID, provider connection, and member permissions |
| Permission denied | Review functional and object-level access with the workspace owner |
| Version conflict | Read the current object and review changes before retrying |
| Changed inputs rejected for a request key | Use a new key for a changed intended operation |
| Only part of a report returned | Follow `next_cursor` with unchanged filters |
| Launch accepted but no objects yet | Read launch and operation status; execution is asynchronous |

## Authorization loop

Check the server URL, automatic OAuth client registration, browser sign-in, and workspace selection. Disconnect the stale connection in **Connections → AI agents**, then authorize again.

If your client asks for a client ID or secret, check that you selected automatic registration. Use the [connection guide](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/connect) for the client-specific setting.

## Tool input error

Use the tool's current input schema. A tool with a `payload` parameter needs its fields inside `payload`; other tools take top-level arguments. UUIDs and provider IDs are not interchangeable.

For insight queries, check the metric, report specification, grain, conversion event, and attribution window with `insights_capabilities`.

For Launcher, use discovery and fresh reads for exact media, creative version, template version, and target IDs. Follow the returned recovery hints.

## Timeout after a write

Look up the action, activity, rule run, or launch before submitting again. A timeout can happen after acceptance. Check the tool's retry instructions and the recorded result before trying again.

## Get help

Include the client, approximate time, tool name, activity or run ID, and error code when contacting [support](https://superlaunch.pro/contact). Exclude passwords, tokens, signed upload URLs, and private campaign data.

# MCP tool index

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/tools

Find all 115 documented MCP tools by task, access requirement, and exact input schema.

This reference covers 115 tools from the reviewed deployed MCP source. Your access, client settings, and enabled features determine which tools you can use. See the [capability overview](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/reference/capabilities) for product workflows.

Use an MCP client with [OAuth authorization](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/authentication). Read tools require `mcp:read`. Write tools also require `mcp:write` and the relevant workspace and target permissions. Preserve argument nesting such as `payload`, `request`, `data`, `family`, and `content`.

Read the [argument examples](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/examples) and [IDs and retries](https://docs.superlaunch.pro/concepts/ids-and-versions) before writes. The schemas define supported inputs; live provider eligibility still requires capability checks and validation.

# MCP argument examples

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/examples

Valid argument shapes for discovery, reporting, campaign validation, memory, and launch polling.

These examples show argument objects for named MCP tools. Send them through your authenticated client. Replace example UUIDs with IDs from discovery reads and generate a fresh request UUID for a new operation.

The read examples do not change advertising objects. `memory_remember` stores a fact; use it only with consent. The campaign example sets `dry_run: true`.

## List accessible accounts

**Tool:** `ad_accounts_list`

Read account IDs, currencies, and time zones before choosing a target.

```json
{
  "limit": 25
}
```

## Read daily campaign metrics

**Tool:** `insights_query`

Replace the account UUID and dates. Call `insights_capabilities` first. Check `complete` and `next_cursor` in the result.

```json
{
  "ad_account_ids": [
    "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"
  ],
  "date_from": "2026-10-01",
  "date_to": "2026-10-07",
  "metrics": [
    "spend",
    "impressions",
    "clicks"
  ],
  "entity_level": "campaign",
  "report_spec": "base_daily",
  "grain": "daily",
  "limit": 25
}
```

## Rank purchase ROAS

**Tool:** `insights_rank`

Choose the purchase event and attribution window that match your analysis. The result distinguishes numeric extremes and includes data-through information.

```json
{
  "ad_account_ids": [
    "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"
  ],
  "date_from": "2026-10-01",
  "date_to": "2026-10-07",
  "entity_level": "campaign",
  "rank_by": "roas",
  "action_type": "omni_purchase",
  "attribution_window": "7d_click",
  "direction": "both",
  "rank_scope": "global",
  "min_spend": 100,
  "limit": 5
}
```

## Validate a paused campaign

**Tool:** `campaigns_create`

This example validates the inputs without creating a campaign. Check `actions_capabilities` first. Review the result before a live request; use a new `request_id` when changing `dry_run` to `false`.

```json
{
  "payload": {
    "request_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002",
    "ad_account_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
    "name": "October traffic test",
    "objective": "OUTCOME_TRAFFIC",
    "special_ad_categories": [],
    "status": "PAUSED",
    "dry_run": true
  }
}
```

## Save a fact after explicit consent

**Tool:** `memory_remember`

Use this only after the user asks you to save the fact or approves that suggestion. Replace the brand UUID and generate a request UUID. Inspect the returned persistence state.

```json
{
  "payload": {
    "request_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002",
    "fact": "Use British English for this brand's campaign copy.",
    "scope": {
      "kind": "brand",
      "target_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003"
    },
    "consent": "explicit_user_request"
  }
}
```

## Find failed tool activity

**Tool:** `activity_list`

Filter by the exact tool name and failed status. Follow `next_cursor` with the same filters to read the complete set.

```json
{
  "payload": {
    "tool_name": "campaigns_create",
    "status": "failed",
    "limit": 25,
    "cursor": 0
  }
}
```

## Discover saved creatives

**Tool:** `launcher_creatives_list`

Inspect saved version details and current eligibility before selecting content.

```json
{
  "limit": 25
}
```

## Poll an accepted launch

**Tool:** `launcher_launches_get`

Use the account and launch IDs from the submission. Use `launcher_run_operations` to check the outcome of each operation.

```json
{
  "ad_account_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "launch_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004"
}
```

## brands_create

Create a brand in the current workspace and grant its creator write access. Supply a fresh request_id UUID. Reuse it with the same payload to safely retry; changed payloads conflict. Optional profile fields are website, industry, description, markets, and languages. No ad accounts are linked.

**Access:** `mcp:read` and `mcp:write`. Workspace and target permissions also apply.

| Parameter | Type | Required / default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `payload` | object | Required |

Keep the argument nesting shown in the schema. Expand it for nested fields, allowed values, and limits.



```json
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "payload": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Create a workspace brand; reuse request_id only for identical retries.",
      "properties": {
        "request_id": {
          "format": "uuid",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "name": {
          "maxLength": 200,
          "minLength": 1,
          "pattern": "\\S",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "website": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "maxLength": 500,
              "type": "string"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null
        },
        "industry": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "maxLength": 200,
              "type": "string"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null
        },
        "description": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "maxLength": 10000,
              "type": "string"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null
        },
        "markets": {
          "items": {
            "maxLength": 100,
            "minLength": 1,
            "pattern": "\\S",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "maxItems": 50,
          "type": "array"

          "items": {
            "maxLength": 100,
            "minLength": 1,
            "pattern": "\\S",
            "type": "string"
```

## brands_update

Update mutable fields on one writable brand. Supply a fresh request_id UUID and at least one field. Reuse the request_id with the same brand and payload to safely retry; changed payloads conflict. Empty markets or languages clear those lists. Use kit to partially update messaging, voice, colors, or typography; a changed kit creates an immutable version. kit.positioning is required when no active kit exists.

**Access:** `mcp:read` and `mcp:write`. Workspace and target permissions also apply.

# Insights tools

Source: https://docs.superlaunch.pro/mcp/reference/insights

Query reports and rank advertising performance.

Check capabilities and current access before a write. Use the exact tool arguments below. Read results before retrying an uncertain provider operation.



## insights_capabilities

List insight grains, compatible metrics, dimensions, and paging semantics.

**Access:** `mcp:read`. Workspace and target permissions also apply.

**Arguments:** none.



```json
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {},
  "type": "object"
}
```





## insights_query

Query one bounded insights page, then follow next_cursor when needed. Call `insights_capabilities` first for valid combinations. The default page contains 25 rows and the MCP maximum is 100 rows to keep tool results within agent context limits. Prefer the default instead of requesting the maximum unless a larger page is necessary. Daily account, campaign, and adset queries automatically roll up aggregation-safe metrics from ad rows; reach and frequency remain exact native metrics at the requested level. Filter structured metrics with `action_types` and `attribution_windows` instead of returning every raw Meta action tuple. Both filters are REQUIRED for actions, action_values, and other structured metrics. For purchase analysis, for example, supply action_types=["omni_purchase"], attribution_windows=["value"]. Choose the action and attribution window that match the question; they are not inferred. Use sorting and `min_spend` before paginating for top-N analysis; use `entity_ids` for targeted follow-up queries.

**Access:** `mcp:read`. Workspace and target permissions also apply.

| Parameter | Type | Required / default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ad_account_ids` | array | Required |
| `date_from` | string | Required |
| `date_to` | string | Required |
| `metrics` | array | Required |
| `entity_level` | account, campaign, adset, ad | `"ad"` |
| `entity_ids` | array or null | `null` |
| `report_spec` | base_daily, demographic_daily, country_daily | `"base_daily"` |
| `grain` | daily, period | `"daily"` |
| `action_types` | array or null | `null` |
| `attribution_windows` | array or null | `null` |
| `min_spend` | number or null | `null` |
| `sort_by` | entity_id, date, spend, impressions, clicks, ctr, purchases, roas | `"entity_id"` |
| `sort_direction` | asc, desc | `"asc"` |
| `sort_action_type` | string | `"omni_purchase"` |
| `sort_attribution` | value, 1d_click, 7d_click, 1d_view | `"value"` |
| `limit` | integer | `25` |
| `cursor` | string or null | `null` |

Keep the argument nesting shown in the schema. Expand it for nested fields, allowed values, and limits.



```json
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "ad_account_ids": {
      "items": {
```
